root_idea.summary: The root centers on bending, curving, and inclination.
root_idea.development: The physical image extends to weight or an affair that bends a person down, yielding the sense of burdening or distressing.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic perfect citation form آدَ rather than the Quranic imperfect يَـُٔودُ.

senses.definition: To burden, weigh heavily upon, or tire someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Transitive Form I. In the Quranic occurrence, the preservation of the heavens and earth is said not to burden or tire God; the object is expressed by a pronoun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become crooked, curved, or bent.
To recede or decline, especially toward evening; to return; of shadows, to return and incline toward the east.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported of the day, evening, things, and shadows in the cited constructions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline toward someone or take pity on him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the construction آدَ عَلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bend, curve, or crook something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive Form I; said of a stick or other thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become crooked, curved, or bent through an extraneous or acquired action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form V; it can also describe bending while rising because of heaviness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In derived constructions: to become burdened or oppressed by a load; to be burdening or distressing; or to be burdened or pressed heavily by a load.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The forms include an intransitive verb and active and passive participles. A related transposed construction is used of an affair pressing heavily upon someone.
Adjectival usage; a feminine form أَوْدَاءُ is also reported.
The word is reported either as lacking a singular or as a plural analyzed in another way.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Recession of the day toward evening.
Decline of the evening is covered by the recession/return branch.
Return of a thing is covered by the same branch.
The shadow construction is included in the recession/return entry.
Transitive burdening/distressing and related derived burden constructions.
Pointer-only entry referring back to Form I.
Form V becoming bent; its Quran citation is used as a grammatical analogy.
Pointer-only entry referring to Form V.
Becoming oppressed or burdened by a load.
Adjectival meaning crooked, curved, or bent.
Active participial meaning burdening or distressing.
Passive participial meaning burdened by a load.
Calamities or afflictions, with disputed singular analysis.

cautions: The Quranic imperfect يَـُٔودُ is presented under the normalized perfect citation form آدَ; the separate intransitive أَوِدَ remains a Classical Arabic meaning and is not merged with the Quranic form.
A Quran reference in the Form V discussion is an illustrative grammatical analogy, not a QAC occurrence of this root.
The root-level lexicon also records أَوْد as a tribal name and أُود as a place-name; the derivation of the tribal name is left uncertain.
